tasks.short: Interview patients about neurological symptoms and history

steps.what: Interview patients about complaints, symptoms, medical histories and family histories

tasks.design: Retain clinical interviewing with the neurologist, referring to {OTHER}, the electronic patient record. A questionnaire or transcript does not remove the need to clarify symptoms, timing and contradictory accounts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients describe neurological symptoms in varied and sometimes incomplete ways.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing patient records provide context for the conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise relevant detail and adapt questions to the patient's account.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust and probe uncertainty without prematurely closing the history.
tasks.altitude: Own the quality of the neurological history.

evidence.claim: Clinical interviewing retains full time; documentation tools do not establish shorter interviews.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic patient record.
The baseline is interviewing and clarification; separate note production is not imported into this task.
Patient and family accounts arise during s1 and are not assumed to be prestructured clinical facts.
No new service is installed, so no automation maintenance is added.
research_questions: Is repeated clerical history capture measurable separately from clinical interviewing?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Clinical questioning and clarification remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Perform neurological procedures and interpret diagnostic tests

steps.what: Perform procedures or diagnostic tests with appropriate patient and equipment checks
Interpret outcomes of neurological procedures, electroencephalography, electromyography and nerve conduction tests

tasks.design: Keep procedure performance and clinical test interpretation with the neurologist using {OTHER}, neurological diagnostic equipment and its clinical record system. Existing signal acquisition and display are retained without claiming them as newly saved labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure safety and interpretation depend on patient condition, artefacts and clinical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing diagnostic equipment supports acquisition and display.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish meaningful abnormalities from artefacts and normal variation.
tasks.human_edge: Combine procedural skill with clinical interpretation.
tasks.altitude: Own reliable neurological testing and interpretation.

evidence.claim: Hands-on procedures and specialist interpretation retain full time; no validated task-specific replacement is established here.

assumptions: OTHER denotes neurological diagnostic equipment and its clinical record system.
The neurologist's s1 includes patient assessment, performance and acquisition checks; s2 uses the resulting recordings.
Where a technologist performs acquisition, that existing work remains outside the focal baseline and is not claimed as saved.
No new automated service is introduced and no added maintenance is incurred.
research_questions: Is any repeated recording transfer distinct from procedure performance and interpretation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Procedure work and interpretation remain; existing acquisition automation earns no new saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order and interpret blood or cerebrospinal fluid laboratory analyses

steps.what: Order appropriate laboratory analyses of blood or cerebrospinal fluid
Interpret results of laboratory analyses against clinical history and diagnostic alternatives

tasks.design: Retain test selection and clinical interpretation using {OTHER}, the electronic ordering and results system. Native order favourites can reduce navigation, but no measured navigation burden or new diagnostic saving is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test selection and interpretation depend on indications, timing and differential diagnosis.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing electronic orders and result views support the workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise when results do not answer the clinical question.
tasks.human_edge: Choose relevant analyses and interpret them in context.
tasks.altitude: Own the clinical purpose and interpretation of laboratory testing.

reach.task: Clarify assay limitations and unexpected results

evidence.claim: Clinical ordering and interpretation retain full time here; order-entry convenience alone establishes no measured saving.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic ordering and results system.
After s1 the laboratory team performs specimen processing and releases results before s2; that existing external labour remains outside this focal baseline without any claimed saving or transfer.
The neurologist's result review and any clarification with the laboratory remain in s2.
No new automation or maintenance is introduced.
research_questions: Can a measured order-entry subtask be improved with native favourites while retaining clinical selection?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Appropriate ordering and clinical interpretation retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose neurological conditions from clinical evidence

steps.what: Diagnose neurological conditions by integrating examination findings, histories and test results

tasks.design: Retain diagnostic synthesis with the neurologist, using {OTHER}, the electronic patient record, to inspect source findings. Interviewing and individual test interpretation remain in their own tasks; diagnosis claims no duplicate saving from them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different neurological conditions can produce overlapping and incomplete evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing clinical records bring source findings together.
tasks.still_hard: Weigh competing explanations and recognise when evidence is insufficient.
tasks.human_edge: Make accountable diagnostic decisions under uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Own the synthesis of evidence into a defensible diagnosis.

evidence.claim: Neurological diagnostic synthesis retains full time in this design; no task-specific autonomous diagnostic capability is established.

assumptions: OTHER denotes the electronic patient record.
Source histories, examination findings and test interpretations arise from their separate clinical tasks; this baseline contains their diagnostic synthesis only.
There is no assumed structured diagnosis flag or automated conclusion.
No new automation service or maintenance is added.
research_questions: Is repeated evidence retrieval a measurable burden outside diagnostic synthesis?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net 0. Diagnostic reasoning remains; separate source tasks receive no duplicate credit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain clinical interviewing, procedures, test interpretation and neurological diagnosis.
reach: Clarify assay limits with laboratory specialists
role.ambitious_version: A neurologist who uses existing clinical systems while retaining accountable clinical judgement and patient interaction.
